interactions.label: General anaesthesia is pharmacologically equivalent to deep natural sleep, diffe

params.question: General anaesthesia is pharmacologically equivalent to deep natural sleep, differing only in the depth of unconsciousness produced.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: General anaesthesia is NOT equivalent to sleep. It is a deliberately engineered state with four specific components: unconsciousness, freedom from pain, amnesia, and complete muscle relaxation. Unlike sleep, anaesthesia abolishes protective airway reflexes, requiring the anaesthesiologist to actively secure the airway.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. General anaesthesia is fundamentally different from sleep. It is a deliberately engineered, reversible state composed of four distinct components — unconsciousness, analgesia, amnesia, and complete muscle relaxation. Under anaesthesia, protective airway reflexes are abolished, which never happens in physiological sleep.

interactions.label: During laryngoscopy, the sniffing position aligns the oral, pharyngeal, and lary

params.question: During laryngoscopy, the sniffing position aligns the oral, pharyngeal, and laryngeal axes. Which combination of movements achieves this alignment?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is reversed. Neck flexion (not extension) aligns the pharyngeal and laryngeal axes, while head extension at the atlanto-occipital joint brings the oral axis into line.

Correct. Neck flexion at the lower cervical spine aligns the pharyngeal and laryngeal axes. Head extension at the atlanto-occipital joint then brings the oral axis into alignment, creating a direct line of sight to the glottis.

answers.text: Full neck flexion with the chin tucked to the chest

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chin-to-chest positioning would severely misalign the oral axis, making visualisation of the glottis impossible. The sniffing position requires head extension at the atlanto-occipital joint, not full flexion.

answers.text: Head extension alone with the neck in a neutral position

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Head extension alone aligns only the oral axis. Without lower cervical neck flexion, the pharyngeal and laryngeal axes remain misaligned, and glottic visualisation is poor.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the three-axis model: neck flexion aligns the pharyngeal and laryngeal axes; head extension at the atlanto-occipital joint brings the oral axis into line. Together they create the sniffing position.
Well done. The sniffing position — neck flexion plus head extension — is the foundation of successful direct laryngoscopy.

interactions.label: Neostigmine is routinely paired with glycopyrrolate when reversing non-depolaris

params.question: Neostigmine is routinely paired with glycopyrrolate when reversing non-depolarising neuromuscular blockade. What is the primary reason for adding glycopyrrolate?

answers.text: It potentiates the neuromuscular reversal effect of neostigmine

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Glycopyrrolate does not enhance reversal at the neuromuscular junction. It is an antimuscarinic agent whose action is at muscarinic receptors, not nicotinic receptors.

answers.text: It accelerates the hepatic metabolism of the non-depolarising agent

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Glycopyrrolate has no effect on the metabolism of muscle relaxants. Non-depolarising agents are cleared by hepatic or renal pathways (or Hofmann elimination for atracurium), independently of glycopyrrolate.

answers.text: It prevents the muscarinic side effects of accumulated acetylcholine

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Neostigmine inhibits acetylcholinesterase, raising acetylcholine at both nicotinic and muscarinic receptors. The muscarinic excess causes bradycardia, excessive salivation, and bronchospasm. Glycopyrrolate blocks these muscarinic effects while preserving the desired nicotinic reversal at the neuromuscular junction.

answers.text: It prevents the re-establishment of neuromuscular blockade after reversal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Glycopyrrolate does not influence whether blockade recurs. Re-curarisation depends on the pharmacokinetics of the non-depolarising agent and the adequacy of reversal, not on antimuscarinic therapy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Neostigmine raises acetylcholine at all cholinergic synapses. At muscarinic receptors this causes bradycardia and bronchospasm. Glycopyrrolate, an antimuscarinic agent, blocks those unwanted effects.
Exactly. Neostigmine raises acetylcholine non-selectively; glycopyrrolate shields the muscarinic receptors from that excess.

interactions.label: During induction of general anaesthesia, preoxygenation with 100% oxygen for 3–5

params.question: During induction of general anaesthesia, preoxygenation with 100% oxygen for 3–5 minutes is performed before any induction agent is given. What is the primary physiological purpose of this step?

answers.text: To increase the partial pressure of oxygen in the alveolar dead space

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Preoxygenation targets the functional residual capacity — the gas that participates in exchange at end-expiration — not the dead space, which does not contribute to gas exchange.

answers.text: To replace nitrogen in the functional residual capacity and extend the safe apnoea time

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Preoxygenation denitrogenates the functional residual capacity, replacing nitrogen with oxygen. This creates a larger oxygen reservoir in the lungs, extending the safe apnoea window from roughly one minute to several minutes and buying critical time for airway management after induction.

answers.text: To prevent absorption atelectasis during positive-pressure ventilation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In fact, high inspired oxygen concentrations can promote absorption atelectasis rather than prevent it. The primary purpose of preoxygenation is to build an oxygen reserve, not to prevent atelectasis.

answers.text: To reduce the minimum alveolar concentration of the volatile agent to be used

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MAC is an inherent pharmacological property of each volatile agent and is unaffected by prior preoxygenation. The purpose is to extend the safe apnoea window, not to alter anaesthetic potency.

overallFeedback.feedback: Preoxygenation replaces nitrogen in the functional residual capacity with oxygen, creating a reservoir that extends safe apnoea time — the window for securing the airway after induction.
Well done. Denitrogenation of the FRC is the single most important safety step before the apnoea of induction.

interactions.label: A 28-year-old non-smoking woman is scheduled for day care laparoscopic surgery w

params.question: A 28-year-old non-smoking woman is scheduled for day care laparoscopic surgery with planned opioid analgesia. Her Apfel score is 4. Which prophylactic strategy is most appropriate?

answers.text: Ondansetron alone administered at the end of surgery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A single antiemetic is insufficient for an Apfel score of 3 or 4. PONV is the leading cause of unexpected admission after day surgery, and high-risk patients require triple prophylaxis.

answers.text: Volatile anaesthetic maintenance combined with intravenous ondansetron

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Volatile agents are themselves emetogenic and should be avoided in high-risk PONV patients. Propofol-based TIVA is preferred for its antiemetic properties, combined with two additional agents.

answers.text: Propofol-based total intravenous anaesthesia, ondansetron, and dexamethasone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. An Apfel score of 3 or 4 calls for triple prophylaxis: propofol TIVA (antiemetic properties), ondansetron (5-HT3 antagonist), and dexamethasone (corticosteroid). This combination addresses PONV through three distinct mechanisms and is the standard for high-risk day care patients.

answers.text: Dexamethasone at induction with metoclopramide at emergence

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Dual prophylaxis is inadequate for this risk level. Moreover, propofol maintenance — an integral part of the triple regimen — is missing. An Apfel score of 3 or 4 mandates three-pronged prophylaxis.

overallFeedback.feedback: PONV is the commonest cause of unexpected admission after day surgery. An Apfel score of 3 or 4 requires triple prophylaxis: propofol TIVA, ondansetron, and dexamethasone.
Exactly. Triple prophylaxis — propofol TIVA, ondansetron, and dexamethasone — is the standard for Apfel scores of 3 or 4.
